A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OpenPros dataset and benchmark. All pages, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison; retained appendix content can be matched across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ultrasound simulations, reconstruction benchmarks, generalization experiments and computational measurements in Figures 3–5 and Tables 4–7.

after.justification: v2 reports revised reconstruction and generalization results, plus original noise-robustness and bone-stratified evaluations in Tables 8–10.

M1.justification: The phantom-generation pipeline, acoustic solvers, reconstruction procedures and neural architectures are retained. Removing the batch dimension from the ViT input-tensor description is a notation clarification, not an architectural change.

E1.justification: The prostate reconstruction task and underlying anatomical coverage remain unchanged. Appendix A.6 adds evaluation with Gaussian-corrupted waveforms, extending input-condition coverage. The bone groups in A.7 subdivide anatomies already represented in v1 rather than introducing new anatomical coverage.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate beamforming, physics-based USCT, InversionNet and ViT-Inversion in the corresponding main comparisons, and retain both learned models in the generalization tests. Newly discussed UNet, diffusion and neural-operator approaches are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 3 revises stated source/receiver spacing from 37.5/3.75 mm to 3.75/0.375 mm. New protocols test clean-trained models with normalized-input Gaussian noise and stratify ID slices by bone involvement. Existing training budgets and OOD splits remain. These reported setting corrections do not establish that simulations were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained OOD tests, v2 adds a controlled noise-sensitivity study for both learned models and quantitative bone-dependent error analysis for ViT-Inversion. Tables 8–10 substantially extend robustness evidence beyond v1's generalization experiments and qualitative bone examples.

E5.justification: Table 4 newly reports means and standard deviations across test slices, with the aggregation procedure explained in Section 4.2. These describe variation across samples, not repeated training runs; neither version supplies seed-based uncertainty or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5 substantially revise scores and reverse the ranking from InversionNet to ViT-Inversion. Table 4 reports InversionNet/ViT RMSE as 0.0433/0.0566 in v1 and 0.0247/0.0205 in v2. Figures 4–5 replace USCT reconstruction panels, and Tables 8–10 add results. These are revised reported outcomes, not established same-setting gains; v2 also contains unreconciled table/prose discrepancies.

T1.justification: The acoustic-wave assumptions, forward/inverse formulation, learning objective and metric definitions are retained. The added Gaussian-perturbation equation specifies an experimental corruption procedure; no theoretical result, proof or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract adds robustness and uncertainty-quantification gaps to the stated findings, and the contribution list explicitly includes robustness testing. The central claims about the first large-scale prostate benchmark, released simulators and learned methods outperforming physics-based reconstruction remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets ID evaluation as interpolation across shared anatomies and positions the simplified dataset as a prototyping benchmark requiring later 3D validation. It also proposes long-range attention as an explanation for noise resilience and suggests mitigation strategies. Existing anatomical-diversity and simulation limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1's resource appendix, containing direct dataset, repository, checkpoint and discussion links plus code/data licenses, is removed. v2 retains the homepage and adds a supplementary-code statement, but loses substantial access and licensing documentation. It newly explains the slice-level 90%/10% ID split and patient overlap, while removing the mask filename category. Resource withdrawal itself is not established.

R1.justification: v2 removes the OpenFWI and EFWI citations and their stated inspirational role, adds Dosovitskiy et al. for ViT and Dai et al. for ultrasound neural operators, and modestly broadens positioning toward other reconstruction model families. Most prior-work coverage remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected introduction, benchmark and discussion passages are rewritten; author/header text and citation style change. Retained appendices become A.1–A.5, and A.8 adds an LLM-use disclosure. The main section sequence and much of the explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially expanded: Figures 4–5 replace USCT panels and revise bone labels, Table 4 becomes a full-width mean-and-standard-deviation display, and Tables 8–10 add robustness and stratified-result displays. The ICLR template also changes typography and layout. Figures 1–3 and 6 retain their underlying artwork.

improvement.justification: New robustness analyses, slice-level variability reporting and clearer evaluation boundaries strengthen v2. However, central results remain unreconciled: Table 4 reports SSIM 0.9955/0.9967, while Section 4.2 gives 0.9877/0.9908. Removing direct resource links and licensing documentation also weakens reproducibility information. These material benefits and harms prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
